newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - gains evaporate near close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - gains evaporate near close.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices lost much of the 1/4 point gains scored at midday and were essentially unchanged to only slightly higher near the close on Friday.
Traders said the afternoon downturn was tied to new speculation that the Federal Reserve's next move will be to tighten interest rates.
That also helped push the Treasury market lower, with the long bond off 1/32 at 96-29/32 to yield 6.74 percent. Munis followed suit, erasing midday gains estimated at about 1/4 to 3/8 point.

"There's a very nervous sentiment developing out there," one market analyst said. The analyst said traders are scared that next week's supply, the first substantial new issue pressure in several weeks, could be problematic.
Next week's new issue calendar is expected to total $2.2 billion in 80 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $806 million in 53 issues. The largest is a $245.8 million two-part Washington general obligation deal on Tuesday.
Negotiated sales total $1.4 billion in 27 offerings. The largest is a $345.7 million Houston refunding deal through senior manager PaineWebber Inc.
In other supply news, the size of New York City's planned bond sale is slightly higher than previously reported, at $850 million instead of $775 million. The deal is expected to price on Jan 14.
In the muni secondary Friday, Florida Port MBIA 5-3/8s of 2027 were bid at a 5.79 percent net, down three basis points from Thursday but off a 5.77 percent quote at midday.
North Carolina Eastern Mountain Power Agency MBIA 5-5/8s of 2024 held on to 1/4 gains, finishing Friday at 98-1/8.

Debt futures lost only some of their gains by the close. The March municipal contract finished the day up 10/32 to 115-17/32. March T-bonds rose 6/32 to 111-18/32, widening the MOB spread between the two contracts to 127 ticks from 123 at the close on Thursday.
